newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian bonds end just up, upside seen.
newsitem.headline: Austrian bonds end just up, upside seen.

text.p: 1530 GMT - Austrian bonds closed just firmer on Thursday and traders said the market had absorbed U.S. inflation data well and predicted further gains to the end of the week.
"The data was well digested and I think we have got room for further upside," said one trader.
U.S. core inflation rose 0.3 percent against a 0.2 percent consensus forecast.
"The market seems to be climbing cautiously upward," said another trader, but noted a tendency towards profit-taking on the buying side.
The German Bund future was well supported at 102,10 points but if support did not hold at this level or at the lower level of 101,90 the market would plummet, the trader added.
The forthcoming Fed meeting next Tuesday and the announcement of a new bond issue were the two factors that could put pressure on the market, dealers said.
* 10 year benchmark 5.75 pct bond maturing July 2006 down up 10 bps at 100.50 to yield 5.68 (5.69) pct in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 100.41/51 to yield 5.69/68.
* Latest five-year 4.375 bond maturing February 2002 closed up five bps at 99.00 in bourse trade to yield 4.61 (4.58) pct, quoted post-market at 98.89/97 to yield 4.64/62 percent.
* Austrian bond future down 12 bps at 109.40 on turnover of 384 lots.
* 10-year spread over Germany steady at minus one, five-year spread up five bps at 15.
* Money market rates steady with three-month VIBOR higher at 3.445 and overnight money steady at 3.10/3.35. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 257
